newsitem.title: USA: Cree Research faces class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Cree Research faces class action lawsuit.

text.p: A class action suit was filed in the United States District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina on behalf of those who purchased common stock in Cree Research Inc between February 1 and July 2, lawyers for the plaintiffs said on Tuesday.
The company had no immediate comment in response to the suit.

On February 1, 1996, Cree said it would produce 1.5 million blue light-emitting diode chips (LEDs) in the fiscal third quarter ending March 31, 1996, and 6 million in the fiscal fourth quarter ending June 30, 1996, according to a statement issued by Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, the law firm representing the plaintiffs.

Following this announcement, the statement said, the company reported record results for its second and third quarters of fiscal year 1996 and continued to say it was successfully meeting its production goals for its blue LEDs.

Against this backdrop of positive announcements, the statement said, the price of Cree common stock rose sharply from $14.125 per share, at the beginning of the class period, to a class period high of $20.625 per share.
After the class period, the stock price declined to $10 per share following the belated disclosure of the facts which had been misrepresented or omitted during all relevant times, the statement said.

The statement said certain directors and officers of the company took advantage of the artificially inflated price by selling substantial portions of their holdings of Cree common stock to the investing public, receiving total proceeds of $3,747,025.
The complaint alleges Cree disregarded the fact it was having significant design problems that lead to cost increases and sales decreases for its blue LEDs.
